boundaries: emit-start to optimizer-enter: BIR/catalog construction (control continues to backend-enter because no optimizer exists).
optimizer-enter to backend-enter: complete transport CPS work including lower-result handoff, not synchronous entry-function return.
backend-enter to source-assembly-enter: JS linking, width validation and effect preparation.
source-assembly-enter to emit-success: source assembly including scalar preparation; scalar-pass-enter is an additional landmark, not an end marker.
limitations: Diagnostic copies only; original expected output SHA is required.
Markers observe actual runtime entry of the selected CPS source-body functions.
Wall intervals include scheduler/runtime and JIT/GC; process.cpuUsage covers all process threads.
Only a handful of marker entry hooks; no per-step timestamps.
No speedup or memory acceptance follows from these timings.
interpretation: These boundaries bracket complete logical CPS intervals between selected source-body entries. They do not use the first return from emit_library_start as a construction endpoint.
The transport interval includes lower-result handoff; source assembly includes scalar preparation. No narrower pure-transform or pure-render claim is made.
Candidate width analysis is entered separately before optimization and again during renderer validation; entry count is not duration.
Every interval uses the same process clock and contributes exactly once to the complete emit span.
Marked copies preserve original bytes plus only the recorded hooks. Both original emitted-output hashes must match.
